global_nkd.assessment: CORRECT. The window closed at 02:55, six and a half hours before the scheduler started at 09:25:31. No slot was ever due. This is not a failure and the audit does not call it one.

roska4_calm.assessment: REAL FAILURE, and it is the day's only true silence. The slot crashed on the column mismatch, leaving a window_open line and nothing else. Both defects behind it (the schema projection and the uncaught refusal) were fixed at 5Q-3 AFTER this slot ran, so it stays failed for the day and is not evidence about the current code.

roska4_stress.assessment: EVIDENCE, NOT SILENCE. Every one of the 24 slots ran and left a NAMED refusal. The window closed cleanly. FAIL is correct under the committed rule (only DECIDED slots count) but it describes a blocked data path, not a broken route. The 5 missing timing rows are the pre-telemetry slots and cannot be backfilled.

roska4_swing.assessment: EVIDENCE, NOT SILENCE, and the cleanest instrumentation of the day: 23 of 23 ledger rows and 23 of 23 timing rows. It refuses on M2K rather than MNQ, which is new information — see new_blocker.

new_blocker.why_a_restart_is_not_enough: SPY_REFRESH_PM fires at 16:20 ET. Restarting the scheduler tonight registers it, but its next fire is 16:20 on 2026-08-25 — AFTER Calm (10:00) and after the whole Stress window (10:35-12:30). Tomorrow's 13:45 pre-flight would also fill the gap, and it is also after both windows. So both windows run tomorrow morning against a CSV that ends 2026-08-21 while the requirement is 2026-08-24.
new_blocker.corroboration: The scheduler's own failure message for this job says the same thing in its own words: 'Tomorrow's Track 1 slots will refuse on regime_csv: stale until it is re-run.'
new_blocker.how_it_would_surface: fresh.evaluate() returns a verdict and does not raise, so a slot with no candidates records decided=true with freshness_allow=false; a slot that wanted to admit a candidate is refused with freshness_refused. Either way tomorrow morning's evidence is not clean.
new_blocker.note: This is a sequencing consequence of B-5R-E's open refresh half, not a new code defect. It is called out separately because the handoff's remedy list implies a restart is sufficient, and measured against the clock it is not.

runtime_timing.p95_gate_verdict: MEASURED BUT MEANINGLESS SO FAR. All 42 runs are early refusals: the slot joins frames, is refused, writes a row and exits. None ran the gate, the candidate search, the admission layer or the explanation writer. 2.8s is the cost of REFUSING, not the cost of DECIDING. The 240s/300s gate cannot be judged until at least one slot completes the full path.
runtime_timing.phase_note: every row carries phases {setup, observe}; setup is consistently ~0.11-0.14s and observe carries the rest.

final_verdict.why: Three of the blockers named this morning are now closed in code and one of them (telemetry) is proven live. But B-5R-D is unrepaired, B-5R-F was measured RECURRING today rather than merely risked, and this audit found a dated consequence of B-5R-E's open half that the existing handoff does not cover: tomorrow's Calm and Stress windows will run against a daily series that is one trading day short, and restarting the scheduler tonight does not fix it because the refresh job fires at 16:20, after both windows.
final_verdict.day_is_judgeable: partly — three sleeves are judgeable and judged; global_nkd is correctly NOT_ENOUGH_DATA_YET; but no sleeve produced a decision, so the day says nothing about the strategy, only about the plumbing.
